# Abstract

This gazetteer compiles settlement population series for the Lower Mississippi Hydrological Unit (HU 08) from 8500BC to 1600AD. Of 68 candidate sites evaluated in the regional ledger, 67 bounded earthwork complexes, salt-dome camps and palisaded towns enter the active settlement inventory, while 1 duplicate coordinate alias within 2 km of Emerald Mound is excluded. The chronology spans from Early Archaic Avery Island (`35` at 8500BC) and Sloan (`55` at 8200BC), Middle Archaic Watson Brake (`480` at 3400BC) and Late Archaic Poverty Point (`1,6k` at 1500BC) through Woodland Marksville (`1,1k`), Troyville (`1,2k`) and Greenhouse (`720`) to Mississippian and Plaquemine capitals led by Parkin (`2,8k`), Emerald Mound (`2,4k`), Winterville (`2,4k`), Bradley (`2,2k`), Lake George (`2,2k`), Nodena (`2,2k`), Carson Mounds (`1,8k`) and Fatherland (`1,8k`).

# Background

Monumental mound construction in HU 08 spans more than five millennia, opening with Middle Archaic earthen ring complexes in Louisiana at Watson Brake, Frenchman's Bend, Hedgepeth, Monte Sano and LSU Campus Mounds followed by Poverty Point [@saunders1997; @gibson2000], and continuing through Middle and Late Woodland geometric plazas at Marksville, Pinson Mounds, Troyville and Greenhouse [@toth1988; @ford1951]. After 1000AD, Mississippian and Plaquemine civic-ceremonial towns proliferated along the St. Francis, Yazoo and Natchez meander belts, matching Kelly et al. [@kelly2025] aggregate radiocarbon summit around 1177AD (`N = 828`) and reaching dense late precontact palisaded nucleation in 1400 to 1540AD [@morse1983; @brain1989; @williams1983].

# Methodology

## Inclusion Criteria and Schema Audit

All 68 candidates in the regional source ledger were checked for WGS84 coordinates, excavated plaza or residential zone bounds and distinct spatial identities. Included records carry regional attribution linked cleanly to their encompassing sub-region and primary site monographs cited here and in the ledger.

## Earthwork and Town Population Calibration

Settlement estimates derive from palisaded village hectares at Parkin, Bradley and Nodena [@morse1983; @mitchem1996], domestic midden arcs at Poverty Point and Watson Brake [@gibson2000; @saunders1997], and mound-plaza residential catchments at Winterville, Lake George, Emerald Mound and Fatherland [@brain1989; @williams1983; @neitzel1965].

# Testing and Validation

Ledger reconciliation and spatial containment checks across all 68 candidates returned `0` errors at GMT+0:

1. **Included Settlements**: 67 sites (`29` in St. Francis-Memphis, `29` in Yazoo-Ouachita and `9` in Natchez-Delta).
2. **Excluded Candidates**: 1 duplicate coordinate and alias record within 2 km merged into Emerald Mound.

# Results

## Top 45 Earthworks and Mound Towns

Table \ref{tab:lm-included} presents the top 45 settlements by peak population descending out of the 67 catalogued sites in HU 08. Earliest occupation appears at Avery Island (`35` at 8500BC, peaking at `280` in 1450AD) and Sloan (`40-55` across 8500-8200BC), followed by Middle Archaic mound complexes at Watson Brake (`480` at 3400BC) [@saunders1997], LSU Campus Mounds (`280` at 3200BC), Monte Sano (`260` at 3300BC) and Frenchman's Bend (`240` at 3500BC). Late Archaic centres peak at Poverty Point (`1,6k` at 1500BC) and Jaketown (`520` at 1000BC) [@gibson2000], succeeded by Woodland mound centres Tchefuncte (`180` at 100BC), Marksville (`1,1k` at 200AD), Pinson Mounds (`850` at 200AD), Ingomar Mounds (`390` at 350AD), Troyville (`1,2k` at 650AD) and Greenhouse (`720` at 600AD) [@toth1988; @ford1951].

Among Mississippian and Plaquemine towns from 1000AD to 1600AD, northern valley centres include Towosahgy (`980` at 1300AD), Lilbourn (`950` at 1200AD), Wickliffe Mounds (`880` at 1200AD), Twin Mounds (`620` at 1250AD) and Obion Mounds (`540` at 1150AD) [@cobb2002], alongside late St. Francis-Arkansas towns led by Parkin (`2,8k` at 1500AD), Bradley (`2,2k` at 1525AD), Nodena (`2,2k` at 1500AD), Carson Mounds (`1,8k` at 1350AD), Upper Nodena (`1,65k` at 1500AD), Chucalissa (`1,35k` at 1400AD), Parchman Place (`1,35k` at 1475AD), Menard-Hodges (`1,2k` at 1600AD), Rose Mound (`1,1k` at 1475AD) and Walls (`1,1k` at 1500AD) [@morse1983; @mitchem1996; @hudson1997]. Yazoo-Natchez-Delta centres encompass Emerald Mound (`2,4k` at 1400AD), Winterville (`2,4k` at 1200AD), Lake George (`2,2k` at 1400AD), Fatherland (`1,8k` at 1500AD), Anna (`1,25k` at 1350AD), Medora-Houma (`920` at 1500AD), Mazique (`760` at 1500AD) and Feltus (`720` at 950AD) [@williams1983; @brain1989; @neitzel1965].

## Excluded Ledger Candidates

One candidate entry out of 68 in the regional ledger is excluded from the active point gazetteer: a duplicate monument-inventory record for Emerald Mound falling within 2 km of the excavated Adams County coordinates, merged cleanly into the primary Emerald Mound series (`750` in 1200AD to `2,4k` in 1400AD) to prevent spatial double-counting.

# Limitations

Borderland sites along the northern Cairo-Ohio confluence and middle Tennessee corridor (such as Kincaid Mounds, Shiloh Indian Mounds and Jonathan Creek studied by Welch [@welch2006]) and central Arkansas River valley complexes (such as Toltec Mounds documented by Rolingson [@rolingson1998]) are assigned to adjacent hydrological units (`HU 05`, `HU 06` and `HU 11`) so shared settlement boundaries are never duplicated. Within HU 08 itself, the remaining 22 catalogued sites below rank 45 - primarily Archaic ridges and smaller Coles Creek or Plaquemine villages peaking between `55` and `380` residents - are retained in the spatial subtraction surface alongside rural density priors [@brain1989; @cobb2002].
